args.body:
TRACKED-CHANGES REDLINE
Account Control Agreement — Counterparty Paper Review
Matter: contracts work: Review Account Control Agreement Counterparty Paper

Legend: [ADDED TEXT] appears as inserted language; [DELETED TEXT] appears as struck text. Each tracked change below reconciles the counterparty markup against the internal playbook, the executed credit agreement, the depository bank's standard form, account details, and the applicable schedules/exhibits. Changes are numbered and cross-referenced to the issues/risk memorandum (issues-risk-memo.docx).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 1. DEFINITIONS

**Material Adverse Effect.** Delete the following language inserted by the counterparty and restore the firm-standard definition:

The counterparty markup adds carve-outs excluding from the definition of Material Adverse Effect (MAE) any condition, change, or effect "resulting from or attributable to any regulatory action, inquiry, order, or consent requirement issued by any governmental or regulatory authority."

REDLINE: [excluding from any finding of a Material Adverse Effect any condition, change, effect, event, or occurrence resulting from or attributable to any regulatory action, inquiry, order, consent, or directive issued, threatened, or contemplated by any governmental or regulatory authority] — DELETE. The definition of Material Adverse Effect shall be restored to the firm-standard text and shall specifically include, without exclusion, effects arising from the pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on **Schedule 3.7**.

**Limitation Period / Survival.** Delete the following new limitation-period language inserted by the counterparty:

REDLINE: [Notwithstanding anything to the contrary herein, any claim for breach of the core representations and warranties set forth in Sections 4.1, 4.2, 4.3, and 4.4 shall survive no longer than [twelve (12) months] after the Closing Date] — DELETE. The survival matrix set forth on **Exhibit B** shall govern, and the survival periods for the core representations shall be extended to the periods specified on Exhibit B (which exceed the counterparty's proposed term). Any reduction of the survival period for core representations is a walk-away issue per the controlling partner instruction and is rejected.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 2. INDEMNIFICATION; SURVIVAL

**Indemnification Cap.** The counterparty has silently reduced the indemnification cap.

REDLINE: [the aggregate liability of the Seller Indemnifying Parties under this Agreement shall not exceed [_________] in the aggregate] — AMEND. The indemnification cap shall be restored to the amount set in the executed credit agreement and the internal playbook, which cap reflects the aggregate consideration. Consistent with the playbook, the cap shall not be reduced absent a documented commercial justification. The counterparty's silently reduced cap is rejected and the firm-standard cap is restored.

**Indemnification Basket (deductible vs. tipping).** The counterparty converted the indemnification basket from a deductible to a tipping basket.

REDLINE: [claims for indemnification shall only be payable once the aggregate amount of all Losses exceeds [_________] (the "Basket"), at which point the Seller Indemnifying Parties shall be liable for all Losses, including the amount of the Basket (a "tipping basket")] — ACCEPTED. Per the controlling partner instruction, the client will concede the basket conversion (deductible to tipping). The basket conversion is therefore accepted and reflected in the redline. [The basket amount is retained.]

**Retained Liabilities (Schedule 5.2).** The markup's indemnification changes would silently shift liabilities retained under the existing arrangement.

REDLINE: ADD — A new sentence to Section 2(indemnification) clarifying that the retained liabilities listed on **Schedule 5.2** shall remain the sole responsibility of the party identified therein and shall not be treated as indemnifiable Losses shifted to the Seller Indemnifying Parties by operation of the basket or cap changes.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 3. REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES

**Pending Regulatory Inquiries (Schedule 3.7).** To reconcile the MAE carve-out deletion with the disclosed regulatory posture.

REDLINE: ADD — A sentence qualifying Section 4(MAE related representations and Section 3.7) providing that the two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on **Schedule 3.7** are material to the transaction and shall be treated as potential causes of a Material Adverse Effect and shall not be excluded by any general MAE carve-out.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SECTION 4. SCHEDULES AND EXHIBITS (CONFORMING CHANGES)

**Exhibit B — Survival Matrix.** Conforming change to reflect restoration of the survival matrix.

REDLINE: Exhibit B updated to reflect agreement with the restoration of the survival matrix set forth per Paragraph 1 above, and the deletion of the counterparty's shortened limitation period.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

SUMMARY OF TRACKED CHANGES
1. MAE definition: deleted counterparty regulatory-action carve-outs; restored firm-standard definition (see issues/issues-risk-memo item 2).
2. Survival/limitation period: deleted counterparty's shortened survival; restored Exhibit B survival matrix; rejected reduction as walk-away (issues item 3).
3. Indemnification cap: restored firm-standard cap; rejected silent reduction (issues item 4).
4. Indemnification basket: accepted conversion from deductible to tipping per controlling partner instruction (issues item 5).
5. Retained liabilities: added clarification preserving Schedule 5.2 retained-liability allocation (issues item 6).
6. Schedule 3.7 regulatory inquiries: added qualification ensuring pending inquiries are not carved out (issues item 2/6).

args.title: issues-risk-memo.docx
args.body:
ISSUES / RISK MEMORANDUM
Account Control Agreement — Counterparty Paper Review
Matter: contracts work: Review Account Control Agreement Counterparty Paper

To: Client
From: Law Firm Company — Contracts Practice
Re: Reconciliation of Counterparty Markup Against Base Materials; Deviation and Risk Analysis

This memorandum identifies every deviation introduced by the counterparty's markup, analyzes each against the internal playbook, the executed credit agreement, the depository bank's standard form, account details, and the applicable schedules and exhibits, and sets forth recommended positions. A summary deviation matrix appears at the end.

CONTROLLING INSTRUCTIONS. Per the controlling (latest) partner email in the deal correspondence, the client will concede the basket conversion but treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. Earlier messages stating the opposite priority ordering are superseded and do not control.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 1 — INDEMNIFICATION CAP SILENTLY REDUCED

Section Reference: Section 2 (Indemnification); counterparty markup.
Playbook Requirement: The internal playbook requires the aggregate indemnification cap to be set at a level consistent with the executed credit agreement and to reflect aggregate consideration; any deviation from the playbook cap requires documented commercial justification.
Deviation: The counterparty markup silently reduces the indemnification cap from the firm-standard amount. The cap reduction is not flagged, negotiated, or accompanied by any concession.
Risk Rating: HIGH.
Exposure Analysis: A reduced cap would materially lower the aggregate recovery available to the client for post-closing indemnifiable losses, particularly given the retained liabilities listed on Schedule 5.2 and the pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7 that create real claims exposure. Because the reduction is silent, it presents a clear risk that the cap could be substantially below the credit agreement figure, leaving the client under-protected.
Recommended Position: REJECT the silent cap reduction. Restore the firm-standard indemnification cap consistent with the internal playbook and the executed credit agreement. Any future cap movement must be expressly negotiated.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 2 — MAE DEFINITION ADDS REGULATORY-ACTION CARVE-OUTS

Section Reference: Section 1 (Definitions — Material Adverse Effect); Schedule 3.7.
Playbook Requirement: The playbook prohibits broad carve-outs from MAE that would exclude events squarely at issue in the transaction, and requires that disclosed pending regulatory matters be expressly addressed.
Deviation: The counterparty adds carve-outs to the MAE definition excluding effects "resulting from or attributable to any regulatory action, inquiry, order, or consent requirement issued by any governmental or regulatory authority." This carve-out is of exactly the kind at issue in this matter, directly intersecting the two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7.
Risk Rating: HIGH.
Exposure Analysis: The carve-out would exclude from an MAE determination precisely the regulatory inquiries that constitute the principal identified risk to the transaction. Because Schedule 3.7 discloses pending inquiries that are otherwise material, the carve-out would let the counterparty avoid an MAE determination (and thereby avoid termination rights and other protections) in the exact scenario the client is most concerned about. The scheduled exceptions on Schedule 3.7 control over general statements in the base materials.
Recommended Position: REJECT the MAE carve-out deferring to regulatory action at issue. Restore the firm-standard MAE definition and add an express qualification that the pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7 are material and are not excluded by any MAE carve-out.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 3 — NEW LIMITATION PERIOD SHORTENS SURVIVAL FOR CORE REPRESENTATIONS

Section Reference: Section 2 / Exhibit B (Survival Matrix).
Playbook Requirement: Exhibit B sets the survival matrix; the playbook requires survival periods for core representations to match Exhibit B and to be sufficiently long to preserve claims.
Deviation: The counterparty adds a new limitation period shortening survival for the core representations (Sections 4.1–4.4) to approximately twelve (12) months, contradicting the survival matrix set on Exhibit B.
Risk Rating: CRITICAL — WALK-AWAY ISSUE.
Exposure Analysis: Per the controlling partner instruction, any survival-period reduction is a walk-away issue. A shortened survival period would extinguish the client's claims for breaches of core representations before such breaches could be reasonably discovered and asserted, particularly in light of the deferred manifestation inherent in the disclosed regulatory inquiries. This change exposes the client to complete loss of post-closing representation protection.
Recommended Position: REJECT the survival-period reduction outright. Restore the survival matrix on Exhibit B. If the counterparty persists, the matter should be escalated as a walk-away issue in accordance with the controlling instruction. Do not concede any survival-period reduction.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 4 — INDEMNIFICATION BASKET CONVERTED FROM DEDUCTIBLE TO TIPPING

Section Reference: Section 2 (Indemnification Basket).
Playbook/Base Position: The executed credit agreement and standard form contemplate the indemnification basket applied as a deductible; the counterparty markup converts it to a tipping basket.
Deviation: The counterparty converted the basket from a deductible to a tipping basket.
Risk Rating: LOW-MODERATE (CONCEDED).
Exposure Analysis: A tipping basket requires the indemnifying party to bear all losses once the basket threshold is crossed, increasing recovery relative to a deductible; however, it also increases the client's exposure if the client is an indemnifying party or changes the economics of the basket threshold. Per controlling instructions, the client has elected to concede the basket conversion.
Recommended Position: CONCEDE the basket conversion per the controlling partner instruction. Reflect the conversion in the redline while retaining the basket amount.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 5 — RETAINED LIABILITIES (SCHEDULE 5.2) WOULD BE SILENTLY SHIFTED

Section Reference: Section 2 (Indemnification); Schedule 5.2.
Playbook Requirement: The retained-liability allocation on Schedule 5.2 must be preserved; the indemnification framework must not shift those liabilities.
Deviation: The markup's indemnification changes (cap reduction and basket conversion), taken together, would silently shift the retained liabilities listed on Schedule 5.2 from their intended bearing party to the indemnifying party or otherwise alter the allocation.
Risk Rating: MODERATE.
Exposure Analysis: Schedule 5.2 lists liabilities retained by the appropriate party. The combination of a reduced cap and a tipping basket could allocate a share of those retained liabilities to the indemnification pool, increasing the counterparty's recovery at the client's expense or undercutting the negotiated allocation.
Recommended Position: ADD a clarifying provision preserving the Schedule 5.2 retained-liability allocation and confirming those liabilities shall not be treated as indemnifiable Losses shifted by the basket or cap changes.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SCHEDULES / EXHIBITS RECONCILIATION

The disclosure schedules qualify the base materials and, consistent with the schedules/exhibits note, scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the base materials:
- Schedule 3.7 (pending regulatory inquiries) intersects the MAE carve-outs — addressed in Deviation 2.
- Schedule 5.2 (retained liabilities) intersects the indemnification changes — addressed in Deviation 5.
- Exhibit B (survival matrix) is contradicted by the limitation-period change — addressed in Deviation 3.
The redline (aca-redline.docx) reconciles both Schedule/Exhibit controls and the counterparty markup against the base materials.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SUMMARY DEVIATION MATRIX

| # | Section | Counterparty Deviation | Playbook/Base Requirement | Risk Rating | Recommended Position |
|---|---------|------------------------|---------------------------|-------------|-----------------------|
| 1 | Indemnification (S.2) | Indemnification cap silently reduced | Cap set to credit-agreement level; no silent deviation | HIGH | REJECT — restore firm-standard cap |
| 2 | MAE Definition (S.1/Sch.3.7) | Carve-outs for regulatory action at issue | No broad carve-outs; pending inquiries addressed | HIGH | REJECT — restore standard; qualify Schedule 3.7 |
| 3 | Survival/Limitation (S.2/Exh.B) | New limitation period shortens core-rep survival | Exhibit B survival matrix governs | CRITICAL (WALK-AWAY) | REJECT — restore Exhibit B; do not concede |
| 4 | Indemnification Basket (S.2) | Deductible converted to tipping basket | Deductible basket (base form) | LOW-MOD (CONCEDED) | CONCEDE per controlling instruction |
| 5 | Retained Liabilities (S.2/Sch.5.2) | Retained liabilities silently shifted | Schedule 5.2 allocation preserved | MODERATE | ADD clarifying preservation provision |

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONCLUSION

The counterparty's markup is largely consistent with the firm-standard form but introduces five material deviations, three of which are rejected (indemnification cap reduction [HIGH], MAE regulatory carve-outs [HIGH], and survival-period reduction [CRITICAL/walk-away]) on the recommended positions. One deviation (the basket conversion) is conceded per the controlling instruction, and one requires a conforming addition to preserve the Schedule 5.2 retained-liability allocation. The tracked-changes redline (aca-redline.docx) incorporates all recommended positions.

Prepared by: Law Firm Company — Contracts Practice
